prediction.likelyOutcome: The estate should prevail on liability for both its trespass/unjust-enrichment counterclaim and against most of Frye's affirmative unjust-enrichment claim, but the Magistrate is unlikely to award the full pled $160,000 given the blended-rate quantification problems and the more specific $1,000/month Commerce Property evidence; expect a net recovery for the estate meaningfully below the ceiling once Frye's largely-documented $25,000 offset is credited.

figures.label: Fair rental value of Dock Street Properties per Mark Raphaelson's testimony
figures.quote: Mark testified that a fair rental value for the Dock Street Properties was $5,000.00.

figures.label: Cleanup cost credit against rent due
figures.quote: The Plaintiff estimated the cleanup would cost around $16,000.00 and testified that he and Mr. Raphaelson agreed that such amount would be taken from the monthly rent due.

figures.label: Blanket demand at $5,000/month combined rate, Jan 2020-Aug 2022
figures.quote: the Defendant counters that the Plaintiff was enriched by using the Dock Street Properties and the Commerce Property from January 2020 through August 2022 without paying rent and seeks compensation of $160,000.00 ($5,000.00 for each month)

figures.label: Documented payment via J.D.A.S., Inc.
figures.quote: Altogether, the Plaintiff, through J.D.A.S., Inc. paid Mr. Raphaelson $25,000.00.

figures.label: Plaintiff's total claimed impoverishment
figures.quote: The Plaintiff argues he has been impoverished, and the Defendant has been enriched, by at least $70,000.00.

outcome.description: The Magistrate's final post-trial report recommended judgment for the estate and against the occupant for $44,000.00 on the estate's unjust-enrichment counterclaim ($1,000 per month for the Dock Street Properties from May 2020 through August 2022, plus $1,000 per month agreed rent for the Commerce Property from April 2021 through August 2022), rejecting the $5,000-per-month / $160,000 demand, denying the occupant's own $70,000 unjust-enrichment claim, and denying the estate's trespass counterclaim; costs to the estate as prevailing party, no attorney's fees.
outcome.appellateChange: none - trial-level magistrate's final report (exceptions available under Court of Chancery Rule 144); no appellate ruling in this document

source.court: Delaware Court of Chancery (Magistrate in Chancery, final post-trial report)
source.excerptNote: Verbatim sentences from Part I (Background, subsections A-F: early years, use and occupancy, attempted purchase, Commerce Property, falling out, procedural history) plus the paragraph of Part II.A that lays out each side's unjust-enrichment demand and the occupant's two responsive arguments. Removed: the introduction and conclusion stating the recommended judgment; every 'I find' / 'I recommend' sentence; the magistrate's rental-value estimate and month-by-month computation; the trespass ruling; footnote citations and record cites. PDF line-break and word-split artifacts were normalized; no wording changed.
